title: Spatial probability field over 32×32 map cells replaces direct (u,v) regression
hypothesis: The naive baseline regresses (u,v) directly from a global-average-pooled feature with MSE. Berlin is full of visually similar places (repeating rooftops, parks, water), so the posterior over position given one 128×128 crop is multimodal — and MSE regression answers a multimodal posterior with its mean, dragging predictions toward the map centroid regardless of what the crop shows. Parameterizing the output as a probability field over a 32×32 grid of map cells lets the model express 'it's one of these few look-alike places' and commit to the strongest mode instead of averaging them. This is the single most decisively supported mechanism in the pre-reset main-branch lineage (its exp 2, kept, 3217→2489 m worst-case; every later champion built on the field family, and all four attempts to replace it were refuted). On this fresh Berlin-daytime-only lineage the same failure mode applies to the same baseline, so the same fix should transfer.
method: In model/model.py only: replace TinyLocNet's 3-way linear head with (a) a field head scoring the 128-d GAP feature against 1024 = 32×32 map cells (~215 m per cell on Berlin's ~6.9 km raster), trained with cross-entropy against a Gaussian-smoothed soft target (σ = 0.75 cell) centered on the true position, and (b) an in-graph decode: sharpened softmax (β = 4) over the field, output = probability-weighted balance point of the cell centers (continuous, sub-cell). The confidence head stays a separate sigmoid linear on the same feature with the baseline's loose BCE ('error < half the map') so the model stays scoreable under the conf ≥ 0.3 / coverage ≥ 0.2 gate. model/train.py is untouched.
expected_outcome: Berlin 'asis' median error (the branch's whole primary metric, single area × single bucket) drops well below the direct-regression baseline's centroid-anchored range (a pure centroid guess on this raster is ~1800 m median; the old lineage's naive baseline scored ~3200 m worst-case). Predicted: ~800–1500 m median. Since best is currently unset (1e18), any finite score is kept and becomes the branch's first champion; the real test is the margin over the centroid floor.
eli5: The old model had to blurt out two numbers — 'you are here' — in one shot. When two parts of Berlin look alike, the safest one-shot answer is to split the difference and point somewhere in between, which is exactly wrong. The new model instead gets a map of Berlin divided into a grid of squares and lights up how much the photo looks like each square — like a game of 'warmer/colder' played on the whole map at once — then commits to the balance point of the hottest region. Saying 'it's probably here, maybe there' and then picking is much more honest than averaging two guesses that are both wrong.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only, no synthetic lighting variants

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: small from-scratch stack of convolution layers that squeezes the crop down to a 128-number summary of what the ground below looks like

stages.name: Location field
stages.detail: the summary is scored against a 32×32 grid of Berlin map cells (~215 m each), producing a heat map over the city: how strongly does this crop resemble each part of the map

stages.name: Decode
stages.detail: the heat map's contrast is turned up and the answer is its balance point — a continuous coordinate that can land between cell centers, not just on them

stages.name: Confidence
stages.detail: a small learned gauge on the same summary predicts whether this fix is trustworthy; fixes below the trust bar are abstained rather than reported

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: instead of being graded on how close its two output numbers land, the model is graded on putting its probability on the true map cell (with a little credit for immediate neighbors); the confidence gauge keeps its old grading

implementation_brief:
ALL changes are in model/model.py. model/train.py is NOT touched — it calls build_model(), loss_fn(model(xb), yb) with yb = (B,2) normalized (u,v) targets in [0,1], and export_onnx(model, path); all three signatures must survive unchanged.

1) TinyLocNet.__init__: keep self.features exactly as is (chans [3,16,32,64,128], stride-2 convs + BN + ReLU, GAP in forward). Add GRID = 32 (module-level constant). Replace self.head = nn.Linear(128, 3) with: self.field = nn.Linear(chans[-1], GRID * GRID) and self.conf_head = nn.Linear(chans[-1], 1). Register a buffer of cell-center coordinates: cs = (torch.arange(GRID, dtype=torch.float32) + 0.5) / GRID; self.register_buffer('u_grid', cs.repeat(GRID))  # (1024,) u varies fastest within each row… concretely build with meshgrid: vv, uu = torch.meshgrid(cs, cs, indexing='ij'); register 'u_grid' = uu.reshape(-1) and 'v_grid' = vv.reshape(-1), both shape (1024,). Convention: cell index k = row * GRID + col, u = x/width ↔ col, v = y/height ↔ row — keep this consistent between the buffers and the loss target.

2) TinyLocNet.forward(x): f = self.features(x).mean(dim=(2,3))  # (B,128). logits = self.field(f)  # (B,1024). p = torch.softmax(4.0 * logits, dim=1)  # sharpened decode, β=4 fixed. u = (p * self.u_grid).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True); v = (p * self.v_grid).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True); conf = torch.sigmoid(self.conf_head(f)). Return torch.cat([u, v, conf, logits], dim=1)  # (B, 1027). The extra logits columns are consumed only by loss_fn and stripped at export.

3) loss_fn(pred, target_uv): logits = pred[:, 3:]. Build the soft target on the fly from the same buffers is not possible (loss_fn is a free function) — instead compute grids locally: GRID=32, cs = (torch.arange(GRID, device=..., dtype=...) + 0.5)/GRID, meshgrid as above, u_grid/v_grid shape (1024,) on target_uv.device. sigma = 0.75 / GRID (normalized units). d2 = (u_grid[None,:] - target_uv[:, :1])**2 + (v_grid[None,:] - target_uv[:, 1:2])**2  # (B,1024). t = torch.softmax(-d2 / (2 * sigma**2), dim=1)  # Gaussian soft target, normalized. field_loss = -(t * torch.log_softmax(logits, dim=1)).sum(dim=1).mean()  # NOTE: log_softmax of the RAW logits, no β — sharpening is decode-only. Confidence term unchanged in spirit from baseline: coord_err = ((pred[:, :2] - target_uv)**2).sum(dim=1); with torch.no_grad(): good = (coord_err.sqrt() < 0.5).float()  # same deliberately loose 'abstain only on catastrophic miss' criterion, now measured on the decoded balance-point coordinate. conf_loss = F.binary_cross_entropy(pred[:, 2].clamp(1e-6, 1-1e-6), good). Return field_loss + 0.1 * conf_loss.

4) export_onnx(model, path): the deployed graph must output shape (1,3) = [[u, v, conf]], NOT (1,1027). Wrap before export: class _Deploy(nn.Module) holding the trained model, forward(x) returns self.m(x)[:, :3]. Export _Deploy(model) with the same dummy = torch.zeros(1,3,128,128), input_names=['frame'], output_names=['uvc'], opset_version=17, dynamo=False. Everything in the deployed path (conv, GAP, linear, softmax, mul/sum, sigmoid, cat, slice) is plain-opset ONNX; no custom ops.

5) estimate_position and build_model: unchanged. Module docstring: keep the export contract sentence intact (1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1] → [[u, v, conf]], u/v normalized map coords, conf in [0,1]); update the 'Baseline:' line to describe the field head.

Fixed contracts to preserve (frozen scorer depends on them): train.py CLI `python -m model.train --area berlin --out-dir runs/<id> [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket N] [--seed N]` unchanged; ONNX at <out>/models/<area>.onnx, input 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output [[u,v,conf]] with u,v in normalized map coords and conf in [0,1]; exported file ≤ 4 MiB (new total is ~370k params ≈ 1.5 MiB fp32 — comfortably inside); single-thread host latency ≤ 250 ms (the added 128→1024 linear + softmax is microseconds). Sanity check after implementing: a random-weights forward pass must produce u,v ≈ 0.5 (softmax near-uniform → balance point mid-map) and finite loss.
